messages.subject: Integrating ggvis with Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am trying to create a map using ggvis that interactively updates the fill attribute based on a Shiny input value. However, for whatever reason, the ggvis will not show up when I run the Shiny app, though outside of Shiny app, it displays just fine. I've copied the server and ui scripts below, and attached them as well.

server.r
# libraries
suppressMessages(library(dplyr))
suppressMessages(library(ggvis))
library(shiny)
library(RColorBrewer)

# create dummy data
base.long <- c(0, 1, 1, 0)
base.lat <- c(0, 0, 1, 1)
test <- data.frame(long = rep(c(base.long, base.long + 1), 3),
lat = c(rep(base.lat, 2), rep(base.lat + 1, 2), rep(base.lat + 2, 2)),
order = rep(1:4, 6), group = rep(seq(1:6), 4)[order(rep(seq(1:6), 4))],
var = rep(seq(5, 30, 5), 4)[order(rep(seq(5, 30, 5), 4))])

# define color palette
spectrum <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(n = 4, name="YlGn"))
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

# determine fill color based on variable
toplot <- reactive({
test$fill.col <- as.character(cut(test$var, seq(10, 30, 5),
include.lowest = T, labels = spectrum(4)))
test$fill.col <- ifelse(is.na <http://is.na/>(test$fill.col) |
test$var < input$range[1] | test$var > input$range[2],
"#FFFFFF", test$fill.col)
return(test)
})

toplot %>%
group_by(group) %>%
ggvis(x = ~long, y = ~lat) %>%
layer_paths(fill = ~fill.col) %>%
scale_ordinal("fill", range = c("#FFFFFF", spectrum(4)),
label = "Variable Value") %>%
set_options(width = 400, height = 600, keep_aspect = T) %>%
bind_shiny("test.ggvis")
})

ui.r
suppressMessages(library("ggvis"))
shinyUI(fluidPage(
sidebarLayout(
sidebarPanel(
sliderInput("range", label = "Filter Range",
min = 5, max = 30, step = 5, value = c(5, 25))
),
mainPanel(ggvisOutput("test.ggvis"))
)
))

Many thanks in advance!
Jane

P.S. In case it is relevant, I am using RStudio on a Mac running OS Yosemite 10.10.

# Export figure data;

)

messages.subject: Re: high cpu load after upgrade to shiny 0.11
messages.subject_clean: high cpu load after upgrade to shiny 0.11
messages.body_plain:
You could try using R's built-in profiling: http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Profiling.html

If it is really pathological you may be able to use my stackdump package (devtools::install_github("jcheng5/stackdump")). You would do stackdump::init(quit=FALSE) at the beginning of your app (say in a global.R), then on the server call "kill -SIGQUIT pid" where pid is the process ID of the Shiny process. This will cause the current execution stack to be printed to stderr. If you're using Shiny Server then you can view the logs at /var/log/shiny-server/*.log to see what is being computed each time you call kill.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny-Leaflet custom marker icons
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yihui,

I echo Stephane's congratulations -- Shiny is a great tool! In combining the leaflet package with Shiny, I found an interesting quirk. When I plotted the code below outside of Shiny, the points all mapped correctly. However, after wrapping in Shiny, it seems that the lng and lat vectors were swapped, such that I needed to specify lng = ~lat, lat = ~long.

In addition, the custom marker no longer imports after being wrapped in Shiny. Is there perhaps something I've done with the JS() command below that is not compatible with Shiny? Again, run in RStudio's console, this code works nicely but once wrapped in shinyServer(), it stops behaving.

m <- leaflet(data = tab) %>% addTiles() %>%
                    fitBounds(lng1 = long[1], lat1 = lat[1], # long and lat are both length 2 vectors; combined, they are essentially a bbox
                        lng2 = long[2], lat2 = lat[2]) %>%
                    addPolygons(lng = ~long, lat = ~lat,
                        fill = T, fillColor = d.fill(), fillOpacity = 0.7,
                        stroke = T, color = "grey", weight = 2, opacity = 0.5)

                if (!is.null(input$layers)) {
                    if (grepl("oaf", input$layers)) {
                        m <- m %>%
                            addMarkers(data = o, lng = ~long, lat = ~lat), # o is a separate dataframe with a set of coordinates
                                 icon = JS("L.icon({
                                     iconURL: 'http://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a6/One_Acre_Fund_leaf.jpg',
                                     iconSize: [10, 10]})"))
                    }
                }

Thank you!
Jane

messages.subject: Too many conditional panels = slow app
messages.subject_clean: Too many conditional panels = slow app
messages.body_plain:
This has come up before:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/slow/shiny-discuss/aKeHTI5pgWU/biyyIla1Uu0J

I often encounter similar issues with larger apps, but it does seem to be specifically due to conditional panels. I think this is what the browser profiling in telling me. Example Firefox in-browser profiling screenshot attached.

Can anyone confirm if this is correct and, if so, is there a better approach to using many conditional panels? I thought doing everything server-side by having all my conditional statements inside my reactive expressions would ultimately be slower. Perhaps there is a point where conditional panels become the bottleneck? Suggestions for best practices? A big app can have a few dozen conditional panels. Even if there is not much data or processing to do; it just seems to be too much conditional logic. Sometimes I will even nest them up to a total of three layers. Is this bad practice? It gives me exactly what I need in certain circumstances, but really slows down the launch of the app, during which time the user cannot interact with the browser in general.

Thanks,
Matt

)

  ui = fluidPage(

    output$map <- renderLeaflet({

  }
)

messages.subject: A few things I learned about shiny (and reactive programming)
messages.subject_clean: A few things I learned about shiny (and reactive programming)
messages.body_plain:
One of the things I really like about shiny is that it has excellent documentation: the tutorial, the articles and the gallery go a long way in helping newcomers as well as intermediate programmers mastering the structure and features of shiny. Still, there are a few things I found lacking from the documentation but important to understand especially if your shiny app is going to be more than just a few lines of R code. I’m sharing them here hoping they can help others avoid some of the roundabouts I took as I learn my way in shiny (follow the link to my blog post to get the detail on each topic below):

Reactive dependencies are dynamic <https://shinydata.wordpress.com/2015/02/02/a-few-things-i-learned-about-shiny-and-reactive-programming/#reactive-dependencies-are-dynamic>
Reactives: order of execution <https://shinydata.wordpress.com/2015/02/02/a-few-things-i-learned-about-shiny-and-reactive-programming/#reactives-order-of-execution>
Use of isolate to prevent accidental dependencies <https://shinydata.wordpress.com/2015/02/02/a-few-things-i-learned-about-shiny-and-reactive-programming/#use-of-isolate-to-prevent-accidental-dependencies>
Conditional panel <https://shinydata.wordpress.com/2015/02/02/a-few-things-i-learned-about-shiny-and-reactive-programming/#conditional-panel>
reactiveValues <https://shinydata.wordpress.com/2015/02/02/a-few-things-i-learned-about-shiny-and-reactive-programming/#reactivevalues>

Does anyone know how to properly initialize the editor extension in a shiny app?

Many thanks in advance.

The response time is virtually instantaneous now.

For context, this is for a huge app with over 40 conditional panels, some nested up to three layers (and much server side conditional reactivity too), eight menus in the navbar, one with nine submenus to individual markdown documents, and with use of navbarPage() nested inside of fluidPage() so that I can still have full control over sidebars and main panels and such based on tabPanel id from the navbar. Also using the new shinythemes package.

Awesome. You guys shaved off all 40 of the 40 seconds lag!

Thanks,
Matt

messages.subject: Re: Pop-up window
messages.body_plain:
Joe Cheng posted the function below for popup's. Of course this coloring would have to work with the built in sorting and search functionality etc.

How can I do this?  Can you alter my code to add the functionality? I am not sure where or what code to write. Can also explain what the callback function is exactly and how it works. Finding this in documentation has been painful. Is there an easier way to do this without callback?

I know i am asking a lot of beginner questions but I hope to learn quickly. Thank you!

messages.subject: Help test next Shiny release
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone -

We're preparing the next release of Shiny, which fixes some layout issues and a performance regression that was introduced in Shiny 0.11. Regarding the performance issue, Shiny should now be even faster than the previous version of Shiny, 0.10.2.2.

If you could test it out and give us feedback, we'd appreciate it!

You can install it with:
  devtools::install_github('rstudio/sh...@v0.11.1-rc')

Here's a list of changes from the NEWS file:

* Major client-side performance improvements for pages that have many
  conditionalPanels, tabPanels, and plotOutputs. (#693, #717, #723)

* `tabPanel`s now use the `title` for `value` by default. This fixes a bug
  in which an icon in the title caused problems with a conditionalPanel's test
  condition. (#725, #728)

* `selectInput` now has a `size` argument to control the height of the input
  box. (#729)

* `navbarPage` no longer includes a first row of extra whitespace when
  `header=NULL`. (#722)

* `selectInput`s now use Bootstrap styling when `selectize=FALSE`. (#724)

* Better vertical spacing of label for checkbox groups and radio buttons.

* The wrapper tag generated by `htmlOutput` and `uiOutput` can now be any type
  of HTML tag, instead of just span and div. Also, custom classes are now
  allowed on the tag. (#704)

* Slider problems in IE 11 and Chrome on touchscreen-equipped Windows computers
  have been fixed. (#700)

* Sliders now work correctly with draggable panels. (#711)

* Fixed arguments in `fixedPanel`. (#709)

* downloadHandler content callback functions are now invoked with a temp file
  name that has the same extension as the final filename that will be used by
  the download. This is to deal with the fact that some file writing functions
  in R will auto-append the extension for their file type (pdf, zip).

Thanks!

messages.subject: DT::Datatable render speed
messages.body_plain:
Hello -- in the code below I am trying to render a dataframe with several records using the old and new datatable elements.  The old datatable renders immediately.  The new one takes 4-5 seconds.  You will need to comment/uncomment sections of the code and run them separately.  Use the slider bar to make a bigger df and obviously the times increase even more, although on my machine the refresh for the old datatable is still pretty much instantaneous.  Thanks.

==============app.R========================
require(shiny)
#require(DT)

MkDF <- function(nr) {
    data.frame(
        varid=sample(10000000:20000000,nr,replace=FALSE),
        description=sapply(1:nr, function(x) paste(sample(letters,10),collapse="")),
        value1=round(runif(nr),3), value2=round(runif(nr),3)
    )
}

server <- function(input, output) {
    ds <- reactive({ MkDF(strtoi(input$nrows)) })
    output$tbl = renderDataTable({ ds() }, options=list(pageLength=10, lengthChange=FALSE, searching=FALSE))

    #ds <- reactive({ MkDF(strtoi(input$nrows)) })
    #output$tbl = DT::renderDataTable({ DT::datatable(ds(), options=list(pageLength=10, lengthChange=FALSE, searching=FALSE)) })
}

ui <- shinyUI(
    navbarPage("Example",
        tabPanel("DT - Old",
            sliderInput("nrows", label=h6("Number Of Rows"), min=20000, max=30000, value=24000, step=1000, ticks=FALSE),
            fluidRow(  column(offset=2, width=4, dataTableOutput('tbl')) )
        )
        #tabPanel("DT - New",
        #    sliderInput("nrows", label=h6("Number Of Rows"), min=20000, max=30000, value=24000, step=1000, ticks=FALSE),
        #    fluidRow( column(offset=2, width=4, DT::dataTableOutput('tbl') ) )
        #)
    )
)

shinyApp(ui=ui, server=server)
===========================================

messages.body_plain:
Vincent was absolutely correct (thanks!) that shiny::renderDataTable()
only implemented server-side processing, and the new DT package uses
client-side processing by default. You can make use of server-side
processing for DT if you can provide a server-side processing function
(as the example on the DT website shows). Please also note that the
server-side processing code here does not even have to be implemented
in R.

Regards,
Yihui

I posted this to Stack Overflow a few weeks ago, but didn't get any help.  My apologies for being redundant if you've seen both.

I am trying to use Shiny and ggvis to:

upload a data set
have the user select 2 columns (x, y)
return a ggvis plot displaying (x, y) from the uploaded data set

I've tried editing the examples from the Shiny Interactivity <http://ggvis.rstudio.com/interactivity.html> page as well as the movie explorer <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/movie-explorer.html> example. However, no chart is displayed.

In the example below, I have simplified this by uploading the mtcars data set and having the x- & y-axes hardcoded (skipping step 2), but it still doesn't work. I think my issue is around uploading the data set, but I don't know where to begin... Any suggestions?

server.R
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)
library(ggvis)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  # uploading mtcars data set
  mtc <- reactive({

    infile <- input$datfile
    dat <- read.csv(infile$datapath,
                    header = T,
                    stringsAsFactors = F)

    if(is.null(infile)) return(NULL)

    dat

    })

  # A simple visualisation. In shiny apps, need to register observers
  # and tell shiny where to put the controls
  mtc %>%
    ggvis(~wt, ~mpg) %>%
    layer_points() %>%
    bind_shiny("plot", "plot_ui")

})

ui.R
library(ggvis)
library(shiny)
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  div(),
  sidebarPanel(
    fileInput('datfile', ''),
    uiOutput("plot_ui")
  ),
  mainPanel(
    ggvisOutput("plot")
  )
))

messages.subject_clean: Formatting and CSS tips for Shiny 0.11
messages.body_plain:
A checkboxGroupInput should have a top margin of 0, and a bottom margin of 25px (by virtue of having class="form-group"). You could use a negative margin if you need to further reduce the space.

One more possibility is that your CSS rules are being overridden by other CSS rules due to CSS precedence rules. As Huidong mentioned, using Inspect Element in the browser can reveal the order in which CSS rules are applied.

-Winston

For examples of server.r + ui.r, see:

-Winston

We've noticed that there's some confusion about whether the server.R needs a call to shinyServer(), and similarly, whether ui.R needs a call to shinyUI(). Shiny app authors might also be wondering why sometimes you can use one file with shinyApp().

To help clear things up, we've posted a new article about this. In the article, we also explain what kinds of things you can give to runApp() to launch an application.

Here's the link:
  http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/app-formats.html

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: invalidate/reset an input value
messages.body_plain:
I'd introduce a reactive variable, and two observers that set it. Like this:

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  v <- reactiveValues(rows = NULL)
  observeEvent(input$rows, {
    v$rows <- input$rows
  })
  observeEvent(datasetInput(), {
    v$rows <- NULL
  })

(observeEvent is newly introduced in Shiny 0.11 and is mostly just a shortcut for doing observe({ x; isolate({y}) }), plus some other convenience features)

Then everywhere you currently refer to input$rows, refer to v$rows instead. v$rows will be set to input$rows or NULL, depending on which observeEvent triggered more recently.

I posted this question a couple of weeks ago on Stack Overflow, but it did not get many views and no one had any answers. I wonder if there might be more interest over here.

I have never been able to make Shiny apps run locally — in any way, shape or form — on the R Studio server on CentOS at our College. Here’s an example. From a fresh R session, enter:
 shiny::runApp(system.file("examples/06_tabsets", package="shiny"))

In the console you get:
 Loading required package: shiny
Listening on http://127.0.0.1:5925

and then a separate browser window opens up. After a moment the UI appears in the window, but before anything appears from the “server” part of shiny, the window vanishes.

A similar problem crops up in related context, e.g., when trying to run a Shiny R Markdown document (either in Pane or in separate window).

Here is the CentOS version info:
    > system("cat /etc/*release*")
    CentOS release 6.6 (Final)
    LSB_VERSION=base-4.0-amd64:base-4.0-noarch:core-4.0-amd64:core- 4.0-noarch:graphics-4.0-amd64:graphics-4.0-noarch:printing-4.0-amd64:printing-4.0-noarch

cpe:/o:centos:linux:6:GA

    [1] C

messages.subject: Re: paging = FALSE of renderDataTable under shiny 0.11 and 0.10.1
messages.subject_clean: paging = FALSE of renderDataTable under shiny 0.11 and 0.10.1
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jie,

Shiny uses the DataTables javascript library.

Shiny version 0.10.1 used DataTables version 1.9.4. With the release of shiny 0.10.2, shiny was upgraded to DataTables 1.10. The names of the table options were changed from DataTables 1.9.x to 1.10.x. Details of the changes can be found here:

http://datatables.net/upgrade/1.10-convert

In your case, the following should work in shiny 0.10.1:

output$testTable <- renderDataTable(iris, options = list(bPaginate = FALSE))

For shiny versions 0.10.2 and higher, the following should work:

output$testTable <- renderDataTable(iris, options = list(paging = FALSE))

There has been some discussion of this change elsewhere in this group: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/shiny-discuss/-0u-wTnq_lA/7YMBzOZDNXUJ

Kevin

messages.subject: Do something with data
messages.body_plain:
I am working through a few of the online tutorials and making changes to them to see how things work. I am quite impressed with the ease of use and functionality so far.

I cannot find an online example for what I would like to try next, and so I am posting my question here.

I am using the two examples that are found within the shiny package below. This is the ui.R and server.R scripts that read in a .csv file. I can modify these in various ways. However, suppose I want to read in the .csv and then do things to it, such as create summaries of variables in the dataframe etc.

Specifically, suppose I want the user to be able to read in any .csv using the code that exists below and then have options to choose any variable in the dataframe, call it x, and then do things such as

sum(x), mean(x), hist(x), lm(y ~ x, data) etc all in the same program.

Any help as I learn this is much appreciated.

Harold

# contents of ui.R

library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$contents <- renderTable({

    # input$file1 will be NULL initially. After the user selects
    # and uploads a file, it will be a data frame with 'name',
    # 'size', 'type', and 'datapath' columns. The 'datapath'
    # column will contain the local filenames where the data can
    # be found.

    inFile <- input$file1

    if (is.null(inFile))
      return(NULL)

    read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep,
                 quote=input$quote)
  })
})

# contents of server.R

library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Uploading Files"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      fileInput('file1', 'Choose CSV File',
                accept=c('text/csv',
                                 'text/comma-separated-values,text/plain',
                                 '.csv')),
      tags$hr(),
      checkboxInput('header', 'Header', TRUE),
      radioButtons('sep', 'Separator',
                   c(Comma=',',
                     Semicolon=';',
                     Tab='\t'),
                   ','),
      radioButtons('quote', 'Quote',
                   c(None='',
                     'Double Quote'='"',
                     'Single Quote'="'"),
                   '"')
    ),
    mainPanel(
      tableOutput('contents')
    )
  )
))

This took a long time to figure out and I haven't found a way to fix it:

If I have an observer that updates the choices available in an input selector based on a reactive function, and that reactive
function has a validate/need block to check for its inputs, then the app crashes and dumps the validate message to the console.
What I would expect to happen is that the observer ignores validate errors, or at the very least replaced the element with the
error message so I knew where the problem happened.

I have not been able to find way to check if a reactive function has returned a validate message and thus prevent the observe
from trying to access the updated value until it has an actual value to work with. Is there a way to get this to work?

I will get you a minimal example just as soon as I sort out the webserver's websocket issue.

messages.body_plain:
The reason it doesn't work with setClass is because shiny.tag is an S3 class, but the setClass function is for the S4 class system.

There shouldn't be anything stopping you from putting tag objects in a list. For example:

a <- div("Tag a")
b <- div("Tag b")

list(
  id = "custom_id",
  component1 = a,
  component2 = b
)

-Winston

messages.subject: get() Plot Properties
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I'm writing an app that displays a phylogeny that the user can interact with.
The phylogeny is plotted and then the user can click on the plot where they would like to zoom on.
So, I'm trying to use the clickId of the plotOutput function, which works fine.
Then I would compare this to the location of different aspects of the phylogeny.
However, what I'm having trouble doing is getting the properties of the plotted phylogeny.
In other similar R functions, the properties of the phylogeny (where the lines intersect, etc.) can be retrieved using get("last_plot.phylo", envir = .PlotPhyloEnv).
I tried using this get function both outside and inside of the renderPlot function, neither of which is able to actually get the properties.
Once a plot is made, is there any way to get these properties like one would in a normal R session?
Any thoughts?

Thanks,
Will

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am using Shiny to visualize some statistics. The UI has to be in multiple languages such that the entire context switches as the language selection is triggered. So this is what I am doing:

I have defined some named lists to store the texts in corresponding languages and I have defined the following select input and slider input fields in ui.R with initial values in a default language:

selectInput("clsLev", clsLevLabel$nl, levList$nl, levList$nl[[3]]),
sliderInput("numRes", numResLabel$nl, min = 10, max = 50, value = 20, step = 5),

Language selection is also controlled by a select input field:

selectInput("lang", langLabel$nl, list("en", "nl", "fr", "de"), "nl")

Accordingly, in server.R I defined an observer to update the two input fields when "input$lang" changes, as follows:

observe({
    updateSelectInput(session, "clsLev", label = clsLevLabel[[input$lang]], choices = levList[[input$lang]])
    updateSliderInput(session, "numRes", label = numResLabel[[input$lang]])
  })

I think I am doing in a right way, however it is very strange that it works only partially: the label of the slider input and the choices of the select input change accordingly, but the label of the select input remains unchanged.

Is there anyone who has also encountered such kind of issue or am I doing it in a wrong way? Any comment or suggestion will be a great help for me. Thank you in advance.

Regards,
Yang

messages.subject: Re: uploaded file path
messages.body_plain:
Apparently, this is impossible.
The fileUpload() function in Shiny is a sort of a Download button in any web browser, which treats the actual file system as a "server".
Due to security issues, it is forbidden for web browsers to have access to the server's file system... therefore getting the actual file path is not possible.

I hope this helps anyone,
Adrian

messages.subject: Re: Customize labels on sliderInput
messages.body_plain:
UPDATE: This does not work anymore with Shiny 0.11.x and creates the warnings

Warnung in if (ticks) { :
  Bedingung hat L?nge > 1 und nur das erste Element wird benutzt
Warnung in if (!is.na <http://is.na>(attribValue)) { :
  Bedingung hat L?nge > 1 und nur das erste Element wird benutzt

However, since Ion.RangeSlider provides a values element for custom labels you can manipulate the input element from R directly and it return it to shiny:

 ticks  <- c(90, 95, 99, 99.9)
 values <- paste0(' data-values="', paste0(ticks, collapse=','), '"/>')
 html   <- sliderInput("foo", min=1, max=length(ticks), ticks=T)
 html   <- sub('/>', values, html, fixed=T)
 html

Note: Setting ticks to TRUE or FALSE does not change the behaviour of the slider. It changes only if all the values are shown under the slider or not. The only limitation seems that elements in ticks should not contain commas since Ion.RangeSlider uses split(",") to decompose the data-values element.

messages.subject: multiconcurrent users cause app crash
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I have some trouble sharing applications with a shiny server open source version.
If only one user launch the app, it works well. If a second user launch the app (on the same computer with another browser or on another computer), the first user app crashes giving the following error : "The application exited unexpectedly. read ECONNRESET"
(it seems that all the connections to the app use the same port)

This problem occurs on very simple apps :

ui.R
shinyUI(fluidPage(
  mainPanel(
    tags$hr(),
    helpText('Test'),
    tags$hr()
  )
))

server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  session$onSessionEnded(function() {
    stopApp()
  })
})

I was told that it was because I share parts of the app out of the app folder but this example doesn't use any extra files.
Thanks in advance for any piece of advice.

messages.subject: Re: multiconcurrent users cause app crash
messages.body_plain:
You're calling stopApp(), which stops the entire Shiny app for all users--that's what it's designed to do. You should never call stopApp in a Shiny Server scenario (at least, I can't think of when it could possibly be useful)--it's intended to be used for Shiny apps that are used directly from an R console, by an R user who can make use of the return value from runApp.

Shiny Server automatically stops Shiny apps a few seconds after the last user leaves, and will automatically start it the next time someone tries to connect. So your shinyServer function for this example should have a totally empty function body.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny apps do not run locally on our R Stduio Server
messages.subject_clean: Shiny apps do not run locally on our R Stduio Server
messages.body_plain:
I have narrowed down the problem somewhat.  When a shiny app runs locally, it writes some files to the /tmp directory.  If after the window disappears (as described above) I leave the app "listening" at its port and then look into the /tmp folder, I do not find any of the files that I find on Linux systems where Shiny apps do succeed in running locally.

Out /tmp directory has the standard permissions:  1777, with only the owner of a file being able to delete it.  So it seems that whatever entity (a shiny server, perhaps?) should be able to write at will into /tmp.

Is there a way to identify the entity that wants to write these files and to grant it the permissions it needs to do so?

>
> I posted this question a couple of weeks ago on Stack Overflow, but it did not get many views and no one had any answers. I wonder if there might be more interest over here.

> Listening on http://127.0.0.1:5925

> and then a separate browser window opens up. After a moment the UI appears in the window, but before anything appears from the “server” part of shiny, the window vanishes.
>
> A similar problem crops up in related context, e.g., when trying to run a Shiny R Markdown document (either in Pane or in separate window).

messages.subject: RPostgreSQL won't deploy to ShinyApps.IO
messages.body_plain:
Hello - Please Help!

My version of RPostgreSQL won't deploy to ShinyApps.IO:
> Preparing to deploy application...DONE
> Uploading application bundle...Error:
> * Unable to deploy package dependency 'RPostgreSQL'
>
>   The package was installed locally from source. Only packages
>   installed from CRAN, BioConductor and GitHub are supported.
> Execution halted

The reason that it wasn't installed from CRAN is that it is incompatible with R3.1.2 and results in this error message when attempting to install from CRAN:
> In file included from RS-PQescape.c:7:
> ./RS-PostgreSQL.h:23:14: fatal error: 'libpq-fe.h' file not found
> #    include "libpq-fe.h"
>              ^
> 1 error generated.
> make: *** [RS-PQescape.o] Error 1
> ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘RPostgreSQL’

So the work-around is to download locally and install the package as source, but then the problem is that it won't deploy to ShinyApps.IO.
CATCH-22

If it makes a difference, I'm on OSX 10.9.5

Can anyone provide some help/guidance?

Thanks,
Isaac

messages.subject: Re: dataTableOutput on Jquery dialog can't work sometimes
messages.subject_clean: dataTableOutput on Jquery dialog can't work sometimes
messages.body_plain:
Shiny generally tries to figure out what outputs are showing, and what outputs are hidden, at any given moment. Any outputs that are hidden, it knows not to recalculate their values on the server--and then when they are later shown, then they will be recalculated again.

The problem is that there's no reliable way for Shiny to know when JavaScript code alters the DOM in such a way that will cause an output to be shown or hidden. So we use the "shown" and "hidden" events as a clue to go examine each output to see if it's now hidden or visible. Many (most) libraries don't raise these events though, so you often have to insert these calls yourself.

messages.subject: Re: RPostgreSQL won't deploy to ShinyApps.IO
messages.body_plain:
Just so we're clear... this is not the type you normally want to use. Your type defaults to "mac.binary.mavericks", which means "Mac OS X Mavericks binaries". The "mac.binary" type means "Mac OS X Snow Leopard binaries". It's only because CRAN doesn't have Mavericks binaries for RPostgreSQL, and we happen to know that the Snow Leopard binaries do work, that makes this OK to do in this instance.

(Also, I was confused by your original email because you said you were installing from source--you weren't. You were downloading the Snow Leopard binary build and installing it, there was no source compiling happening. When repos=NULL, then type is mostly ignored.)

messages.body_plain:
In that case, in ui.R but before you start your UI definition, load the dataset:

mydata <- read.csv("path-to-file")

Then the selectInput choices attribute would be something like unique(as.character(mydata$foo)), where "foo" would be the column name you want to use.

messages.subject: Re: Gray Screen
messages.body_plain:
Carrie,

I am assuming you are talking about your application on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, right? In that case, and for future issues, you will be better off to post your questions to the following forum:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/shinyapps-users

Application connections time out after a certain period of inactivity. This is by default 15 minutes, but you can change that value in the shinyapps dashboard:

Application -> Settings -> Advanced -> Connection Timeout

If you or your users see a different behavior, then please provide more details about the issue:
- Application URL
- How long application is up before it greys out

Best,
Fereshteh

Could someone post a complete example or tutorial of some kind on this? It seems like an essential functionality, to be able to freeze 1 or more columns in a data table. messages.subject: Re: Customize labels on sliderInput
messages.body_plain:
Hello Sigbert,

I tried your code but I wasn't able to get it work correctly. The surprising thing is that it's working when I remove the "#" in the commented line.

ui <- pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Slider labels"),
  sidebarPanel(
#     sliderInput("foo2", label = "slider 1 :", min = 1, max = 4, value = 1),
    uiOutput("slider")
  ),
  mainPanel()
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$slider <- renderUI ({

    ticks  <- c(90, 95, 99, 99.9)
    values <- paste0(' data-values="', paste0(ticks, collapse=','), '"/>')

    html   <- sliderInput("foo", label = "slider 2:", min=1, max=length(ticks), ticks=T, value = 1)

    html   <- sub('/>', values, html, fixed=T)
    html

  })
}
runApp(list(ui = ui, server = server))

Thanks for your help,
Matt

messages.subject: Re: Collapse Shinydashboard box from server.R
messages.body_plain:
Sorry, there isn't a simple way to do this right now. You could still use Javascript to trigger a click event -- you just need to use the right selector.

This will find the first box with a collapse button and trigger it.
  $('.box').find('[data-widget="collapse"]').click()

This still isn't ideal, because the box itself doesn't have an ID, so if you have multiple boxes with collapse buttons, you'll have to do a little more work to pick out the right one, by numeric position, or perhaps by finding one with a particular title associated with it. This is still all doable with jQuery, but will require a little more work.

-Winston

output$download_report <-
        downloadHandler(filename = 'Report.pdf',

                        content = function(file){

                          rnw <- normalizePath('Report.Rnw')

                          owd <- setwd(tempdir())
                          on.exit(setwd(owd))
                          file.copy(refer, 'refer.bib')

Dear all,

I am coming back to this "old" thread....

I was using the helpPopoup function over the last versions of shiny, but it seems that shiny 0.11 does not support the function anymore.

Here is the code for your review:

helpPopup <- function(title, content,
                      placement=c('right', 'top', 'left', 'bottom'),

                      trigger=c('click', 'hover', 'focus', 'manual')) {

  tagList(
    singleton(
      tags$head(
        tags$script("$(function() { $(\"[data-toggle='popover']\").popover(); })")
      )
    ),
    tags$a(

      href = "#", class = "", `data-toggle` = "popover",
      title = title, `data-content` = content, `data-animation` = TRUE,`data-html` = TRUE,

      `data-placement` = match.arg(placement, several.ok=TRUE)[1],
      `data-trigger` = match.arg(trigger, several.ok=TRUE)[1],

      tags$i(class="icon-question-sign")
    )
  )
}

I would be very happy to get any ideas.....

Thank you in advance

Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: How can I stop renderplot from blinking?
messages.subject_clean: How can I stop renderplot from blinking?
messages.body_plain:
Just to be clear about what this is doing:

We consider it a feature, that Shiny makes partially transparent any output that is being recalculated. This is so that when the user moves a slider to a new value, they don't mistake an old plot output for the correct updated value.

This style tag just undoes that effect by overriding the rule that we put in for lowering the opacity, specifically for a single input. You can also remove the "#output_id" section if you want to override this effect for ALL outputs in a Shiny app.

messages.body_plain:
Btw, the solution comes via CSS3 'column-count': http://www.w3schools.com/css/css3_multiple_columns.asp

And custom CSS in Shiny (I chose the method: 'add to header' of UI with 'tags') http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/css.html

i.e.

## here's the top of your ui.R file

shinyUI(fluidPage(

 ## custom CSS for 3 column layout (used below for mechanics filter options)
  tags$head(
    tags$style(HTML("

     .multicol {

       -webkit-column-count: 3; /* Chrome, Safari, Opera */

       -moz-column-count: 3; /* Firefox */

       column-count: 3;

     }

   "))

 ),

## use the css, assuming your long list of vars comes from global.R

   wellPanel(

     tags$div(class = "multicol", checkboxGroupInput("foo", choices = your_vars, label = "foo", selected = NULL))

   )

))

messages.subject: shiny and javascript direct communication
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm creating a rather complex user interface using a vector graphics library such as Raphael.js
Shiny works well with (and is reactive to) various html inputs like text, radio, checkboxes, listboxes etc.

I was wondering: is it possible to make a custom Javascript code "talk" with R via shiny?
A procedure like:
- something happens on the screen, due to a javascript code
- the user does something interpreted by the Javascript code
- the Javascript code asks something to R via shiny
- R responds back (via shiny) to the Javascript code, e.g. returning a JSON text object
- the Javascript code does something on the screen

Would that be possible?
I still very much like the way shiny can produce outputs and graphics, but I would still need a bit more flexibility to create custom communication protocols.

Thanks very much,
Adrian

messages.subject: Re: zoom, pan, and axis rescale
messages.body_plain:
Think of Shiny as a way to wire up user input with R calculations, and route the results into web-based output widgets. Shiny is so agnostic about how you choose to present results that it isn't really meaningful to talk about a generic notion of panning and zooming in Shiny. However, you can use panning/zooming JavaScript libraries with Shiny (there's a packaging issue <https://github.com/bokeh/bokeh/issues/554> with bokeh specifically that currently makes that integration difficult, but dygraphs, leaflet, highcharts, and others can be used in Shiny apps using their respective R packages).

On Wednesday, February 25, 2015 at 11:07:17 PM UTC-8, Paul Lemmens wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> I am getting quite curious why it seems to take such an effort to enable panning and zooming in Shiny. There are also R packages like rbokeh and dygraphs that support zooming in on a plot out of the box (i.e., without specifying anything in a function call). Is this some kind of limitation in Shiny or is it more that Shiny is so generic that you really need to go to the lower level (like mentioned above) to get this worked out?
>
> Thanks for your input!

messages.body_plain:
(add shinyapps-users, remove shiny-discuss)

Wow, bizarre:

> This function uses the MaxEnt species distribution model software, which is a java program that you can download here. Put the file ’maxent.jar’ in the ’java’ folder of this package. That is the folder returned by system.file("java", package="dismo"). You need MaxEnt version 3.3.3b or higher. Please note that this program (maxent.jar) cannot be redistributed or used for commercial or for-profit purposes.

You could try including that jar file in the root directory of your app, then in global.R copy the file from "maxent.jar" to system.file("java/maxent.jar", package="dismo"). But I wouldn't be surprised if it fails to copy due to permissions. It would be easy if the dismo package could provide an option that lets you provide your own location for maxent.jar.

messages.subject: Developing Shiny Apps with Multiple Monitors
messages.subject_clean: Developing Shiny Apps with Multiple Monitors
messages.body_plain:
What are some best practices on developing Shiny apps (or more generally anything in R) using multiple monitors for RStudio Server? I understand RStudio Server does not support multiple monitors yet so I'm looking for workarounds that members of this forum employ. (FYI I couldn't find an RStudio Server Google Group, so posting here because it's relevant to Shiny as well).

I sometimes open R Studio on one screen while editing other files with text editors but I would be more productive with RStudio Server's features. I'm thinking about how I'd go about creating multiple logins / home directories and using git to merge changes from each screen but this seems extreme. Thoughts?

Thanks,

Chris

P.S. While I'm posting questions about RStudio Server -> I can't get Alt+- to work in Firefox (which is the only browser to decently support Hidpi in ubuntu....) as mentioned here <https://support.rstudio.com/hc/communities/public/questions/201761763-Assignment-operator-shortcut-not-working-with-Firefox-RStudio-Server->. Does anyone have a solution other than binding "<-" to a different hotkey using a third-party software package like Autokey?
